content_note: Every rule here is intent-only: a name, an id and a logic line that names the detections the rule would join. There is no query, schedule, severity or alert mapping, so nothing in this file can be imported into a tenant as-is. Author the rule in the XSIAM console from the logic line.

rules.logic: Analytics("ITDR-018 Remote Usage Of An Azure Service Principal Token From Off-Baseline Infrastructure") AND Analytics("ITDR-018 Attempted Azure Application Access From An Unknown Home Tenant") AND ABIOC("ITDR-018 Unusual Resource Access By An Azure Application Deviating From Learned Baseline") joined on the SHARED app id carried in identity.claims.appid within 900 seconds. The remote token replay, the unknown-tenant cross-tenant access, and the unusual resource-access burst all carry the same abused service-principal app id, so the three Azure Audit Log analytics alerts fuse into a single identity-owned ITDR incident whose causality anchor is identity.claims.appid — remote token replay -> unknown-tenant access -> unusual resource access — presented to the DC as end-to-end evidence of the stolen service-principal-token storyline.
rules.name: ITDR-018 Azure Service-Principal Token-Abuse Identity-Owned Incident Stitch
